questions.q: How did Passepartout feel about his master's plan to rescue the young woman?
choices: He was charmed and began to love his master
He thought it was foolish and wanted to leave
He was afraid and begged Fogg to give it up
He agreed only because he was paid extra
questions.evidence: He began to love Phileas Fogg.

questions.q: Why did the guide agree to help with the rescue?
choices: Fogg promised to give him the elephant
He and the woman were both Parsees
He was afraid of Sir Francis's soldiers
He had once worked for the woman's father
questions.evidence: I am a Parsee, and this woman is a Parsee

questions.q: What was the name of the young woman who was to be sacrificed?
choices: Kiouni
Pillaji
Aouda
Bundelcund

questions.q: According to the guide, what was the young woman's background?
choices: She was a servant girl from a village near the pagoda
She was the daughter of a rich Bombay merchant, educated in English
She was a princess raised in the palace of the old rajah
She was a traveller from Calcutta who had been kidnapped on a train
questions.evidence: the daughter of a wealthy Bombay merchant

questions.q: Why did the party decide the rescue had to happen during the night?
choices: At daybreak she would be led to the pyre and no one could save her
The elephant could only travel safely after dark in the forest
Sir Francis had to be back with his troops before the morning
The guide said the temple doors were always unlocked at night
questions.evidence: the abduction must be made that night

questions.q: What did the party find when they first crept up to the doors of the pagoda?
choices: The doors were open and the temple was empty
Guards with naked sabres were watching at the doors
A crowd of priests was singing on the steps
The rajah's soldiers were asleep beside the doors
questions.evidence: were watching at the doors and marching to and fro with naked sabres

questions.q: After waiting until midnight with no change among the guards, what did the party decide to do?
choices: Return to the elephant and ride to Allahabad
Make an opening in the rear wall of the pagoda
Bribe the guards with money from Fogg's bag
Wait in the trees for the sacrifice to begin
questions.evidence: an opening in the walls of the pagoda must be made

questions.q: What tools did the party have for breaking through the temple wall?
choices: An axe and a crowbar from the elephant's pack
Only their pocket-knives
The guide's long hunting knife and a spade
Iron bars taken from a window of the pagoda
questions.evidence: the party only had their pocket-knives

questions.q: What stopped the party while they were loosening the bricks?
choices: A cry was heard inside the temple, and then guards came to the rear
The wall turned out to be solid stone that their knives could not cut
Passepartout fell and made a loud noise that woke the sleepers
Heavy rain began to fall and put out all the torches
questions.evidence: suddenly a cry was heard in the interior of the temple

questions.q: The text says, "The tranquil Fogg waited, without betraying any emotion." What does "tranquil" mean here?
choices: Calm and quiet
Nervous
Angry
Puzzled and lost
questions.evidence: The tranquil Fogg waited, without betraying any emotion.

questions.q: When Sir Francis said they should go away, why did Fogg want to stay?
choices: He said he was not due at Allahabad until tomorrow before noon
He said the guards would surely fall asleep before morning
He said he had already paid the guide to finish the job
He said he had made a bet that he would save the woman
questions.evidence: I am only due at Allahabad tomorrow before noon.

questions.q: Where was Passepartout while he worked out his idea?
choices: Hiding behind the funeral pyre
Lying beside the sleeping elephant
Perched on the lower branches of a tree
Crouching by the stream near the pagoda
questions.evidence: perched himself on the lower branches of a tree

questions.q: When Sir Francis grabbed Mr. Fogg's hand at dawn, what did he find in it?
choices: A pistol
An open knife
A small torch
A coil of rope
questions.evidence: found in it an open knife

questions.q: Who was really the "rajah" who rose from the pyre and carried the woman away?
choices: The old rajah, who had not been dead after all
Passepartout, who had slipped onto the pyre in the smoke
The Parsee guide, wearing the rajah's robes
Sir Francis, who had crept around behind the crowd
questions.evidence: It was Passepartout himself, who had slipped upon the pyre

questions.q: How did the party know their trick had been discovered as they rode away?
choices: A ball whizzed through Phileas Fogg's hat
The elephant was hit by an arrow in the leg
The priests blew horns all through the forest
Soldiers on horses blocked the road ahead
questions.evidence: a ball which whizzed through Phileas Fogg's hat

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: Fogg buying an elephant to cross a gap in the railway
The daring rescue of Aouda from the funeral pyre
Sir Francis telling the history of the pagoda of Pillaji
Passepartout being arrested for entering a temple
questions.evidence: had delivered the young woman from death
